text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- Kapers, the union of Swissair cabin personnel, is protesting against the airline's hiring of some 120 flight attendants from Thailand, Korea and India for certain flights, saying it will negatively affect salary and contract negotiations.
- Heinrich Gattiker, diplomat and representative of Switzerland to the European Council, died last Friday after injuries suffered in a bicycle accident in Strasbourg.
- Unemployment offices in Switzerland reported 197,732 jobless persons at the end of April, an increase of 4,475 persons or 2.2 percent over the previous month.
- Because of its acquisition of the Mercantile & General Re in 1996, Swiss Re has become the world's leader in life and health insurance.
- Gotthard Bank announced it acquired a 74.875 percent stake in Geneva's Banque de Gestion Privee.
- The U.S. is giving Christoph Meili, the Swiss security guard who was fired from his job after sneaking out historical bank documents from Union Bank of Switzerland, a green card.
Meili said that although his family has received threats since the incident, Swiss officials have done nothing to help them.
- Globus department stores suffered a huge loss for the 1996/97 fiscal year due to its loss in market share, despite a 10.6 percent increase in group sales.
- The World Economic Forum has ranked Switzerland sixth out of 53 countries in terms of economic competitiveness. Singapore and Hong Kong are still at the top of the list.
- Currency experts expect that the U.S. dollar, now hovering around Sfr 1.41, will climb to well over 1.50 in 1998.
- The Swiss government wants to charge 40-tonne trucks, which will be allowed to travel through Switzerland starting in year 2005, an average of 460 Swiss francs per truck.
